name: Mogao Caves (Caves of the Thousand Buddhas)
description: Network of 492 cave sanctuaries carved into a cliff at the Silk Road junction of Dunhuang, housing 45,000 square meters of Buddhist murals.
history: Served as a spiritual nexus for merchants, pilgrims, and scholars traveling the Silk Road across the Gobi Desert.
construction: Carved into sandstone conglomerate cliffs, decorated with mineral pigments including lapis lazuli, malachite, and gold leaf.
architecture: Contains colossal seated Buddha statues up to 35 meters tall and the secret Library Cave (Cave 17) holding ancient manuscripts in multiple languages.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the world's richest repository of Silk Road art.
currentStatus: Protected in Dunhuang, Gansu Province, China.
